newsitem.title: PERU: Names of some released hostages wrong - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Names of some released hostages wrong - Red Cross.

text.p: Names of seven of the 225 men freed from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima did not match those on an official Red Cross list of hostages to be released, the Red Cross said on Monday.

"Two hundred twenty-five people left, and 218 of them correspond to the list of names. We are trying to establish the identity of the remaining seven to resolve the incongruence," a Red Cross source told Reuters.

The Red Cross official said the mystery over the names could be explained in several ways. One possibility is that some men invented false names from the start of the siege last Tuesday and came out under those names.
It is also possible that some hostages left the compound using the name of another hostage, who remained inside the residence, he added.
But it cannot be ruled out that a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebel left the residence hidden in the large hostage release on Sunday, the source said.
The discrepancy in the lists would explain confusion over the whereabourts of the Bolivian ambassador.

His name was among those of freed hostages read out by the Red Cross on Sunday, but Bolivian Embassy officials in Lima said on Monday that envoy Jorge Gumucio was still being held inside the compound.
